newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dealers see new trading range for Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Dealers see new trading range for Singapore shares.

text.p: Share prices in Singapore could move their trading range up a level over the next two weeks as a firm opening to the market on Tuesday maintained the upward momentum of Monday's close, dealers said.
"We're seeing a little bit of a breakthrough, now we've got to see if we can maintain it," one dealer said.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 9.20 points at 2,214.89 at 0240 GMT, a firm response to Monday's close above the 2,200 level after the previous week was spent testing it.
"I wouldn't be surprised now if we get through the 2,250 level in the next week or two," the dealer said.
Another record high on Wall Street again provided Singapore with an early morning push, said dealers, who now expect local and regional funds to attract strong interest during the day.
"I think we're seeing fund managers beginning to scramble around to get back in to Singapore and increase their weightings where they were light," said one dealer.
Monday's debut share, interior design firm Nobel Design, brokerage Kim Eng Holdings and engineering company Armstrong Industrial were early volume movers at 0240 GMT.
